newsitem.title: FRANCE: Broker values Airbus at $15-18 bln - paper.
newsitem.headline: Broker values Airbus at $15-18 bln - paper.

text.p: U.S. broker Lehman Brothers reckons European aircraft group Airbus would be worth $15 to 18 billion if it is converted into an autonomous corporation from its current four-nation cooperative status, Le Monde paper said on Saturday.

Airbus Industrie, a four-way partnership between state-owned Aerospatiale of France, Spain's CASA, Daimler Aerospace amd British Aerospace, plans to change to a corporation but has yet to say how it will do this.
The evaluation was the first carried out in the 25-year history of the Airbus grouping and contained in a research piece by Lehman analyst Joseph Campbell, Le Monde said in its weekend edition.

"Airbus is now profitable and should remain so in the future. The European group has reached the critical size which will allow it to amortize its research and development costs more easily," Le Monde quoted the Lehman study as saying.

The analyst also said a merger between Airbus and U.S. group McDonnell Douglas could allow Airbus to take 50 percent of the global market, which Boeing currently dominates with a 60 percent share, Le Monde said.

The analyst also said Airbus could soon take the first step towards becoming an autonomous corporation be announcing the creation of a "collective-name company", a legal structure that would be a prerequisite for the fully fledged conversion, the newspaper said.
